title: Surge Attenuation Gateway for Heterogeneous Canary Handshakes
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a new Surge Attenuation Gateway that smooths abrupt traffic increases during staged promotions; integrates with rollback-oracle to auto-quarantine cohorts when SLOs degrade. Backwards-compatible with existing rollout policies.
description:
Summary: Implements a lightweight "Surge Attenuation Gateway" that sits in the rollout control plane and mediates sudden traffic spikes during heterogenous staged promotions (canaries, A/B lanes, shadow funnels). Motivation: we've seen two incidents where an aggressive promotion + uneven cohort distribution caused transient overload on smaller model variants and downstream caches. This PR introduces a policy layer that enforces handshake pacing, per-cohort "grace tokens", and a short-term smoothing window so downstream allocators and model pools can stabilize before full cutover.

What it does (high level):
- Introduces a new controller component (RolloutGateway) that enforces surge budgets and handshake backoff.
- Adds per-cohort "grace tokens" allocated from a global surge budget; tokens are consumed when a cohort receives ramped traffic and replenished on cooldown.
- Adds deterministic session-affinity passthrough so sessions started during attenuation keep consistent routing until a safe commit.
- Integrates with the existing rollback-oracle: if telemetry gates trip during the smoothing window, the gateway triggers an autonomous quarantine and fast-rewind path.
- Exposes metrics and traces for surge_budget_used, cohort_backoff_seconds, handshake_failures, and attenuation_decisions to the console.
- Adds a small e2e smoke harness (simulator) that can replay synthetic bursts to validate smoothing and rollback behavior.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc and simulation results attached (Linear ENG-4123)
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] End-to-end smoke replay harness added
- [x] Backwards-compatible config (existing rollout specs ignored if gateway disabled)
- [x] Observability: dashboards, Grafana queries, and alert snippets included
- [x] Runbook notes for SRE and on-call (linked)

Commits (summary):
- feat(gateway): initial controller scaffold + policy engine (3 commits)
- feat(metrics): expose attenuation metrics and tracing spans
- feat(sim): synthetic burst replay harness and test cases
- fix(ci): adjust integration test timeout and flake guard
- docs(runbook): add playbook steps for attenuation-induced quarantines

Files/areas changed (high level):
- services/rollout/controller/gateway.go (new)
- services/rollout/policy/attenuation_engine.go (new)
- services/rollout/sim/smoke_replay.go (new)
- proto/rollout/v1/gateway.proto (new messages for metrics + API)
- telemetry/metrics_definitions.yaml (metrics + alerts)
- docs/runbooks/attenuation_playbook.md (runbook)
- tests/integration/rollout_gateway_test.go (integration tests)
- pkg/session/affinity.go (minor change: preserve affinity during attenuation)
- api/rollout/README.md (usage examples and config)

Testing performed: unit tests (100% for new package), integration tests against local docker-compose allocator, simulated burst e2e runs (100+ runs across different cohort size distributions). Observability validated by creating dashboard panels showing metric behavior during a synthetic surge: surge_budget_used tracks expected consumption; cohort_backoff_seconds increases for smaller cohorts.

Telemetry and alerting: added Grafana alert rule (alert: SurgeAttenuationHighUsage) that fires when surge_budget_used > 90% for 2m. Added an SLO guard that surface 'attenuation_quarantine' events to the rollout SLO channel.

Runbook (short): when attenuation quarantine occurs, SRE should: check the 'attenuation_decisions' trace, inspect cohort latency/rate changes, and if the rollback-oracle recommends auto-rewind, verify snapshot integrity and then execute the snapshot rewind playbook. The runbook contains manual override steps to bypass gateway for emergency cutovers.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Arjun Patel (reviewer): "Nice approach; can you clarify interaction with autoscaler? If gateway holds traffic, will autoscaler over-provision?"
  - Author reply (Maya): "Gateway exposes a short-lived 'attenuation window' header so autoscaler receives capped RPS signal; we also added an integration test to cover this. See tests/integration/rollout_gateway_test.go:TestAutoscalerSignal."
- Lena Rodriguez: "Please add a schematic showing token flow and replenishment policy in docs."
  - Author: "Added diagrams to docs/runbooks/attenuation_playbook.md and a small inline ASCII diagram in gateway.go header."
- Samir Kapoor: "Edge case: what if cohort affinity identifiers are ephemeral and can't be relied on? Might lead to session drift."
  - Author: "We fallback to token-bound sticky cookies for ephemeral cases and mark session as best-effort sticky; documented tradeoffs in README."

Requested changes and resolution: 
- Increase integration test timeout for noisy VM CI: done (ci fix commit).
- Add a feature flag to disable gateway globally: done (config flag rollout.gateway.enabled=false).
- Explicitly warn in Release Notes about potential transient error spikes while smoothing runs for large fleets: added.

CI: All checks passed on final run: unit (pass), integration (pass), lint (pass), gosec (pass), proto-gen (pass). A flaky test in early runs was traced to simulated clock drift in test harness and was fixed by deterministic clocks in sim.

Performance impact: Microbenchmarking shows attenuation adds a median 0.6ms to control plane decision latency (acceptable for rollout windows). No changes to token path or inference path were added; this is strictly control-plane logic.

Telemetry examples (console queries):
- rollout.surge_budget_used{env=prod,region=us-east-1}
- rollout.cohort_backoff_seconds{cohort_id="canary-42"}

Compatibility & migration notes: Existing rollout specs are untouched unless the operator enables the gateway. For Dedicated/private installs, the gateway can be configured as a sidecar or centralized controller; documentation added for both patterns.

Why this is different from previous mechanisms: instead of abrupt on/off treats, Surge Attenuation Gateway enforces a smoothing policy that considers global budget, cohort sizes, and downstream allocation signals, reducing noisy rollbacks and improving stability for heterogenous model fleets.

Merge notes: Squash-merged into main after approvals from Arjun, Lena, and Samir. Merged with CI green and post-merge smoke run completed on staging.

Follow-ups (planned):
- ENG-4198: add adaptive budget tuning via historical workload patterns.
- ENG-4301: expose per-customer attenuation telemetry for enterprise tenants.

Links: Linear ENG-4123 (design + sim), docs/runbooks/attenuation_playbook.md, internal dashboard draft (grafana/dashboard/rollout-attenuation.json).
notes: This PR was driven by a pair of incidents in Dec-2025 where rapid promotions caused small variant thrash.
Authors: Maya Chen (lead), paired with Samir for policy tests.
Staging release included a canary run for 48h with no regressions; metrics recorded.
Feature flag rollout.gateway.enabled=false by default for initial e2e consumption.
